citation.authors: Martin ZT, Akins JD, Merlau ER, Kolade JO et al

cited_by.title: Sauna and heat bathing: heart health, recovery and risks

record.population: Eighteen healthy young females: nine Black (average 21) and nine White (average 27), United States
record.design: Single-session experiment: 60 minutes of whole-body heat therapy in a tube-lined hot-water suit (49 degrees C water), vascular tests before and 45 minutes after
record.finding: Before heating there was no difference in vascular function between the groups. Heat improved forearm blood flow response and brachial artery flow-mediated dilation in both groups (6.2 to 8.8 per cent), with no effect on cerebral vascular reactivity.
record.note: The only heat-therapy study in Black participants I found. It used a hot-water suit instead of a sauna, one session, in young women. It shows a short-term vascular response and no health outcome.
